issues: TypeScript compilation error: src/screens/ReceiptEntryScreen.tsx references getAllReceipts but does not import it, causing TS2304 (Cannot find name). Also arrow function parameters have implicit any types (arr, r). Fix by adding import { getAllReceipts } from '../../src/lib/receiptStore' and typing callbacks.

CSV export verification line format does not match the required "# verification: entries=<N>, headHash=<HASH>, code=<CODE>" format. The current implementation appends a simple CSV line "<N>,<HASH>,<CODE>". Update generateCsv to prepend "# verification: " and use the correct key names (entries, headHash, code) as expected by tests.

appendEntryForExport in src/lib/ledger.ts stores an incorrect code (concatenates 12‑char code with the entry hash) and does not correctly record headHash. The ledger entry's data.code should be exactly the 12‑hex‑character verification code, and data.headHash should be the hash of the newly created export entry (i.e., the entry's own hash). Adjust the function to set data.code = code12, compute entry hash, then set data.headHash = entry.hash, and store the entry accordingly.

CSV export verification line parsing in tests expects the line to start with "# verification:" and contain the fields "entries=...", "headHash=...", "code=...". After fixing generateCsv to produce the correct format, ensure that the verification line includes these exact labels and the 12‑character code, not the combined code.

Export.created ledger entry tests (M11) expect exportEntry?.data?.code to match /^[0-9a-f]{12}$/ and data.entries/headHash to be correct. The current appendEntryForExport produces a longer code and missing entries/headHash fields. Update ledger export entry creation to conform to R28 (fields format, code, entries, headHash).

CSV export verification test (M7) expects verificationLine to start with "# verification:". Current generateCsv does not include this prefix. Adjust generateCsv to generate the verification line accordingly.

PDF export (src/lib/exportPdf.ts) uses appendEntryForExport with the same flawed implementation, leading to failing tests for PDF export verification code length and ledger entry fields. After fixing appendEntryForExport, PDF tests will pass.

verifyExportCode in src/lib/exportVerification.ts currently matches the full code (12‑char + hash) and may not work after fixing export entry code length. Ensure it matches only the 12‑character code stored in entry.data.code. The logic already checks e.data?.code?.toLowerCase() === codeNorm, which will work after fixing the ledger entry.

Potential missing ledger initialization for first launch imports (R11) may not be correctly handling duplicate imports. Ensure initLedgerIfNeeded marks imports as done and does not create duplicate "imported" entries. Tests for import (M7) currently fail because import may not run or duplicates may occur. Review ledgerHelpers implementation to correctly add exactly one imported entry for each existing receipt and mileage record on first launch and set a flag to prevent repeated imports.
feedback: The current implementation does not compile and fails multiple acceptance tests, mainly due to incorrect ledger export handling and CSV verification line format. Fix the TypeScript errors, adjust the export ledger entry to store the correct fields, update CSV/PDF generation to emit the required verification line, and ensure import-on-first-launch logic correctly creates exactly one imported entry per record. After these changes, re-run tests and re-validate type checking.
